text:
evan (sales): Heads-up: Vectorly migration POC starts tomorrow. Customer needs a drop-in replacement for their /v1/query and /v1/extract endpoints. Ask: maintain existing UX for search+extract, match billing model (bundle calls), and respond to procurement security checklist. Priya, can you lead the technical presales work?

priya (solutions): On it. Draft checklist: 1) adapter request/response contract 2) tokenization delta sample run 3) prompt envelope preservation 4) error semantics + retry mapping 5) parity harness + metrics 6) pricing conversion scenarios 7) security Qs answered.

lee (eng): Adapter approach: lightweight Go proxy that accepts Vectorly payloads, rewrites to Redwood API, and returns wrapped responses. We'll: header map, param defaults, and token normalization pass. Example mapping:
# client -> adapter: POST /vectorly/query {"q":"<PROMPT>","max":300}
# adapter -> redwood: POST /v1/complete {"input":"<PROMPT>","max_total_tokens":300, "stop":["\n\n"]}
We ran an initial 100-sample set and saw ~+7% token delta. We'll run 200 samples for confirmation.

norma (security): Procurement wants: EU residency, KMS/HSM, per-customer audit logs, and IP allowlist for staging. Quick answers: EU region pinning supported for Private; CMKs via AWS KMS supported for Dedicated/Private; HSM via partner integration on request. We can export audit logs (S3). Send their checklist.

evan (sales): Uploaded the procurement sheet and highlighted residency, HSM proof, SLA for POC, and liability language for hallucinations.

cory (sales-eng): Pricing: Vectorly sells call bundles. Options to propose: A) token-equivalent with +7% adjustment B) flat-call equivalence using measured avg tokens C) migration credit for first month. I'll prepare 3 invoice examples for 60k calls/month.

elle (cs): Canary plan: synthetic parity run (same prompts), then route 5% live traffic for 12h with failback to Vectorly on >=2 errors/5m. Monitor exact-match %, structured extraction F1, and token-length delta. Collect diffs in CSV for triage.

lee (eng): Response deltas usually from tokenizer vocab & sampling defaults. Mitigations: force temp=0 for deterministic outputs in POC, inject explicit stop tokens, and normalize whitespace/punctuation in post-process. Adapter will include a small token-offset table to align billing.

priya (solutions): Eval harness: small node script to call both endpoints, record tokens and outputs, then compute metrics: token_delta, exact_match_rate, structured_f1, length_delta. We'll produce JSONL so product can triage failures.

norma (security): Action: I'll draft answers for the procurement sheet (EU pinning, KMS answers, audit log details) by tomorrow noon. Need the highlighted questions and any custom legal phrasing.

evan (sales): Legal is looped for DPA/HSM addendum.

infra-bot: Canary scheduled: vectorly-adapter -> canary-2026-04-01T09:00Z (5% traffic). Checks: unit tests, tokenizer-run, parity harness.

priya (solutions): Action items: 1) 200-sample tokenizer run -> priya (EOD) 2) adapter stub + mapping doc -> lee (tomorrow 09:30) 3) procurement answers -> norma + legal (tomorrow noon) 4) pricing examples -> cory (tomorrow COB) 5) parity harness -> priya + lee (initial by day 1 of POC) 6) canary runbook & failback -> elle (pre-canary).

evan (sales): Quick sync 08:45 tomorrow for 10m. Ping here if blocked. :thumbsup:
